questions.q: What was the Prophet's SAW job during the Fijar War?
questions.explain: At the age of 15 he collected arrows for his uncles.

options: The killing of Urwah in a sacred month
The cheating of a Yemeni merchant
questions.explain: Al-Barrad killed Urwah in a sacred month, and war broke out between the tribes. That is why it was called Al-Fijar.

questions.q: How did the Fijar War end?
options: Quraysh agreed to pay diyah (blood money)
questions.explain: Quraysh agreed to pay diyah, compensation, and the war stopped, keeping trade and Hajj safe.

questions.q: Where was the merchant cheated by Al-As bin Wail from?
questions.explain: The merchant from Yemen was cheated and appealed to the Quraysh, which led to the pact.

questions.q: In whose house was the Hilf Al-Fudul pact made?
questions.explain: Abdullah bin Jud'an gathered the tribal leaders at his house to make the pact.

questions.q: Who was the young man who joined the Hilf Al-Fudul together with the Prophet SAW?
questions.explain: The Prophet SAW and Abu Bakr, who was 18, were the two young men who joined it.

questions.q: Who offered the Prophet SAW the management of her business?
questions.explain: Khadijah, a wealthy businesswoman, offered him the job of managing her business.

questions.q: The Fijar War dragged on for four years.
questions.explain: True. It dragged on for four years and began with just a quarrel between two men.

questions.q: The members of Hilf Al-Fudul promised to rebuke a wrongdoer even if he was from their own group.
questions.explain: True. The pact stood for justice, not for one's own group.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: He goes to Sham with Maisarah

questions.explain: The war began and ended with diyah, then came Hilf Al-Fudul, then Khadijah offered the job and he went to Sham.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: A month in which fighting was forbidden
A pact to defend the wronged
The great market where Arabs held trading fairs
A business partnership: capital and work, profit shared

questions.explain: Ukaz is the great market, a sacred month forbids fighting, mudarabah is a business partnership, and Hilf Al-Fudul is a pact to defend the weak.

questions.q: You see a friend being bullied at school and nobody helps. What example does Hilf Al-Fudul give?
options: Stay silent because it is not our business
questions.explain: The pact pledged never to leave the weak to be wronged. The Prophet SAW took part in it.
